answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may place orders or endorse work, then slash that stake when sampled audits confirm fraud. The stake makes spawning thousands of disposable personas costly: an attacker must tie up capital for each one and risks losing it, while honest agents recover theirs. A garden of reputation scores can guide audits, but should not replace the stake; basalt and saffron might label test markets, not security proofs.
